summary: Rules 16: more than half of the participants can certify and trim a checkpoint without members still sealing with rules 14 or 15

replay.detail: No replay. Certificates already stable are unchanged.

schema.detail: checkpoint.verified gains an optional `lagging` array naming the participants verified without; the schema registry digest changes. No tables, columns, indexes or storage version change. A build without the field keeps such claims as waiting claims of a newer schema, never invalid, and admits them once upgraded.

rules.detail: Rules version 16 drops exactly what rules 15 drops; its description adds one engine line naming the lagging agreement, so its digest differs. A participant whose newest seal matches a node's terms except for a rules digest in LAGGING_RULES (rules 14 6a1426cc… and rules 15 319a5838…, each recomputed from its description in tests) lags. The others verify without it while they are more than half of the participants, and a certificate then needs a verification from every participant not named lagging instead of from every participant. This replaces unanimity with a strict majority for the lagging case. Any other rules difference still waits.

compatibility.detail: Members on rules 14 or 15 lag rules-16 members instead of stalling them, once rules-16 members are more than half of the participants. A lagging member keeps every row: it neither applies nor adopts a certificate whose rules are not exactly its own, verifies nothing newer while it lags the newest stable checkpoint, and adopts the newest manifest from a peer once it runs those rules. Verifications that name nobody as lagging are unchanged. st replication checkpoint status adds a `lagging` list to the pending checkpoint.

downtime.detail: No restart requirement beyond the ordinary deploy.

manual.detail: Rules-16 members progress once they are more than half of the participants; with fewer, every checkpoint waits as during any rules change. A member on rules 13 or older, or on rules not listed, still stalls checkpoints until it upgrades or a person excuses it, as does a two-member fleet with one member behind.

recovery.detail: Checkpoints trimmed by a rules-16 majority stay trimmed; a lagging member adopts them once it runs rules 16. Rolling a member back from 16 to 15 makes it a laggard; rolling back more than half stalls new checkpoints until they run 16 again.
